analysis:
The PR changes documentation only: hardware-support.md (lines 534-541) and inference.md (hunk at 956-991). No code, key handling, attestation, wire or authorization behavior changes. The docs describe a startup shape warmup that runs probes and cells in the idle calibration session, with a 20 s wall budget and a foreground-lease preemption path. It publishes no observations or work totals. The proactive MLX pool sweep waits while a session runs, and on-pressure reclaims still run.

Threat-model relevance:
- T-010/T-029 (availability) and the TB-007 memory model: warmup uses the same KV and service budgets and cannot lower activation or OS reserves. It is preemptible by customer requests, and the 20 s budget bounds it, so no new DoS surface is evident. Running warmup in preload before registration is bounded by the registration gate timeout.
- T-041 (prefix cache/TTFT oracle): warmup prompts are synthetic and use default sampling. The docs do not state whether warmup donates to the SSD prefix cache or under which cacheSalt. If warmup prompts were donated or hit, they would enter the at-rest cache or the timing oracle. The docs do not address this, so the implementation should be checked. It is unverified and the code is not in the supplied evidence, so I record it here rather than as a finding.
- T-028 (residual GPU memory): warmup traffic is not consumer data, so there is no new plaintext exposure.
- Env var DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP=0/always is a local operator knob forwarded by the launchd job. It is not a trust-boundary change.

No security regressions identified in the supplied documentation. Source-level review of ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmup and the sweep gating is out of scope for this change.
